messages:
sam: Heads-up — onboarding opt-1.2 (fp8 hybrid) to the canary pool. Quick smoke: table-extract and csv ingestion tests look fine overall but seeing an odd XML/CSV quote bleed on a few legal-parsing prompts.
ashok: Can you paste a minimal failing example?
sam: Sure — this one converts a doc with embedded XML snippets into CSV rows. The output sometimes fuses closing tags into the next field: `... </note>,"John Doe"` becomes `</note>,"John Doe</note>"` in a couple cases.
li: Ugh, sounds like tokenizer boundary nonsense or a byte-level truncation. Is the failure deterministic?
dana: I ran the same prompt 10x on opt-1.2/awq-int8 variant — 3/10 showed tag bleed, all with long inline code blocks.
sam: Here's the exact prompt I used:
```
Convert the XML document into CSV rows: <row><id>123</id><note>value, with comma</note></row>
```
and the model output for the bad run: `123,</note>,"value, with comma</note>"`
ashok: Interesting. Could be a combination of our post-tokenization escape logic and how the model emits `</` as a token when using fp8 attention approximations.
dana: Also saw a small uptick in hallucinated citation tokens when the same runs used quantized KV cache (warm start). Not big, but measurable on the legal-qa eval set.
li: Can you add the token-level diffs? A short snippet from the token stream around the boundary would help.
sam: Attaching a paste from the canary run (trimmed): `..., 134, 27, 409, 5, 2, 3, 1024, 7, 90, 409, 11, ...` — the `409` token seems to change role between runs.
ashok: 409 maps to `</` in the vocab? If that aligns then small quant noise could flip following delimiter tokens.
dana: Quick repro plan: 1) run deterministic seed with no batching, 2) run canonical tokenizer check (round-trip), 3) run raw logits compare between fp8 and fp32 for the boundary tokens.
li: I'll kick off 1 and 2. @deploy-bot can you pin a canary build with opt-1.2/fp8-no-kvcache and opt-1.2/fp32 for direct compare? :eyes:
deploy-bot: canary deployment queued — opt-1.2/fp8-no-kvcache -> pool-a; opt-1.2/fp32 -> pool-b. ETA ~6m.
sam: Thx. Also let's add CSV-aware prompts in the eval harness to catch quote bleed ASAP.
ashok: If fp8 kernel is collapsing subtoken boundaries, a mitigation might be to force-escape `</` into the input as `</` pre-tokenizer for structured-object tasks. Ugly but fast.
dana: I'd prefer a targeted post-processing patch first (detect `</` inside quoted field and unescape) while we root-cause the kernel behavior. Low-risk.
li: Agree. I'll run token diffs and post a short table of mismatched logits. If the diffs cluster near the delimiter token, that's a smoking gun.
sam: For traceability, adding a new regression alert in Redwood Optimize: tag `schema-escape-bleed/opt-1.2` with the failing prompt set.
ashok: Good. Also add a canary that disables prefix KV caching — earlier runs suggested warm cache increased incidence.
dana: Notes: frequency ~0.3 on long-doc table tasks, zero on short prompts. Also correlated with heavy punctuation density.
sam: OK — continuing triage. Will post logs and token diffs when ready. Thanks all :thumbsup:
li: ping when diffs are up, I'll try a tiny quant re-run with altered rounding mode.
ashok: If we confirm kernel-level rounding issue, we should notify runtime team and label a hotfix candidate.
dana: Filed eval ticket #EVAL-8312 and added the failing set.
sam: Closing loop: next update in this thread after the logits compare.
